value.first: For 3am wakings I'd use graduated check-ins (the Ferber method). It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and the skill it builds, falling asleep alone, is exactly what he needs to fall back asleep at 3am. Pick a calm week with no travel or illness. Do the same 20-30 minute wind-down nightly, with the feed before the book, then put him down drowsy but awake and leave.
value.second: When he cries, wait before going in. Night 1: 3, 5, then 10 minutes, and 10 for every check after. Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15. Checks last 1-2 minutes, lights off, same calm phrase, a pat at most, no pickup, no feed. Treat a 3am waking like bedtime and restart that night's waits from the first one. Nights 4-7: 12/15/17, then 15/17/20, 17/20/25, 20/25/30. Expect 30-60+ minutes of protest, and night 2 or 3 may be worse. That's the old habit breaking.
value.third: If you can't stand timed waiting, the chair method (sitting beside the crib, moving the chair away every 3 nights) is gentler but slower. Giving in at minute 9 teaches longer crying, so decide ahead who handles checks. It's working when he falls asleep faster and 3am settles. Call the doctor if you notice snoring, gasping or pauses in his breathing, or signs of pain like ear-pulling or fever. I'll check in Thursday.
